newsitem.title: UK: RTRS-Gold likely to plunge to US$365 by year end -UBS analyst.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Gold likely to plunge to US$365 by year end -UBS analyst.

text.p: Gold prices are likely to plunge to $365 by the end of the year after a surge in speculative short positions on Comex on Monday, the fourth largest in 10 years, a leading analyst said on Thursday.
The market would first, however, most likely see a short-covering rally before collapsing to the fresh lows, Andy Smith of Union Bank of Switzerland told Reuters.
"These things don't go down in a straight line, although we've had 11 straight falls on Comex. You'd expect at some point a covering rally," he said.
Open interest shot up by 11,950 lots on Monday and by 4,570 more on Tuesday to a total of 186,183.
"This was...the fourth biggest move to the short side (falling price/rising open interest) in the last decade or so," Smith also wrote in a commentary issued mid-week.
The others occurred in January and July 1995 and August 1991.
The big investment funds were now on the short side after having been largely behind a blistering rally to six-year highs around $418 early in the year which lasted about five weeks.
"Is that the same sort of time scale for this short selling? I don't know, but I think it's not going to be over in days," Smith said.
According to Smith's research, in the three previous cases of huge short selling, prices were slightly weaker one and two months following the short moves.
"History shows whatever covering rally you get it doesn't last a month or two months," he said.
There were several factors that could pressure prices in coming months, .
The International Monetary Fund is meeting on Friday to discuss selling a small portion of its gold reserves, but wrangling could carry on for months.
Gold producers, who earlier in the year liquidated hedges, are now exposed against a fall in price and may nervously re-enter the forward selling market, Smith said.
"It's on a knife-edge to that extent. The support from the producers we've had through most of this year could turn 180 degrees if we do break down," he said.
In Australia, a recent rejevenation of the domestic currency, coupled with weaker dollar gold, has pushed local gold prices to new lows for 1996, below A$480, Smith said.
Physical buying usually increases when prices break out of a range as fabricators lock in prices, but then it subsides.
"That's why we haven't collapsed, the first break down through $385 saw buying, but once that's done they stand back and wait," Smith said.

After the shake-out, however, Smith expects gold to rally in early 1997. "The New Year is a wonderful time to take a fresh look at things...my gut feeling is that we will have a washout before a rally."
